item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I meant -1s abducting gaurds, not the Foundation nabing a resident. I agree that the risk/reward ratio isn't favorable for a snatch-and-grab.

But the gaurds should all be forewarned, because they should be reading these procedures. So they should know that the residents can flip hostile without warning. They should be handling themselves like doctors and orderlies in an institution for the criminally insane; calm and friendly, but on constant alert and prepared for an attack from anywhere at any time. I'm not saying the gaurds should be able to defend themselves every time, but once in a while the seasoned professional fighter should be able to escape from the untrained mob.

I also don't think it would be as hard to camouflage a secure perimeter as you think. Just put most of your fortifications on the inside of the wall. A wide, deep ditch would stop most things a suburban neighborhood could bring to bear, and if you stretch some light tarps across the top the perpetual snow will hide it for you.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
The main issue with them being taken down is that they aren't forewarned. They're just walking along and then they're being tackled from behind.

Regarding the -1's, I'm still unsure as to why they would want to grab one in the first place. They're apparently completely normal humans who just love Christmas to the point of ridiculousness. Getting ahold of one would require them to run in, grab somebody who does not want to be grabbed, and then haul them out while being assaulted by an army of maniacs. Just to get a look at somebody who really likes Christmas. They have no reason to want to get ahold of one, and they'd risk a breach to do so. I don't know how that would pay off, and I can't see them justifying risking the lives of a significant group of personnel just to get a look at an apparently normal guy.

The -1's could get out of anything that could reasonable be passed off as a neighborhood. Ladders are rather popular as a decorating assistant during the holidays, and I'm sure there'd be plenty in the average neighborhood.

The whole containment deal is part of trying to look inconspicuous. It's the difference between 'oh look, some people having a friendly party' and 'holy shit they are gassing a mob of people'.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I like everything about this.
It is thoroughly amusing and seems light-hearted, and then you think about it for just a second and there is this whole ocean of stepford creepy just below the surface.

I have just two very minor notes/questions.
1) It seems the -1s are physically normal. I can see them managing to swarm and take down a gaurd who didn't know about their tendency to flip hostile without warning, but how do they consistently manage to overcome trained soldiers who are forewarned? Could be addressed in-article by mentioning unsuccesful abduction attempts, where the "scrooge" got away.
2)Why can't we just lock them in to prevent the monthly carousing? A properly designed security gate wouldn't attract any outside attention, and could stop even the jolliest yule-zombie without risking personel the way slipping them a mickey does. They would probably get agitated, but they wouldn't be able to spread and just give the neighbors the same coverstory the next morning. For that matter, why not skip directly to the gas every time? Less risk of one slipping through and if done quickly there would be very little risk of exposure.

item.content:encoded:
From the description, it sounds like the community's residents only ever leave during Noel events, so:

1) Since it seems that the don't have jobs, how do they pay for electricity and other utilities?

2) Where do they get the supplies for eggnog? (And for other food, presuming they ingest anything besides eggnog)

3) Do they keep re-exchanging the same gifts over-and-over, or are the all gifts given new? If the gifts are always new, where do they come from, and how come the community isn't entirely cluttered with gifts?

For #2 and #3, it could be that the Foundation doesn't know, but they'd make a note that they don't know how it happens.

SCP-784 will always be covered by between 12 and 33 centimeters of snow, though no unseasonable weather will occur above SCP-784.

Shouldn't they somehow mess with satellite images, so no one using Google Maps notices?

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I don't really like this. There's a large number of issues with tone and the like, things like "sweaters commonly associated with gift giving" which tells me exactly nothing, "eggnog related festivities" - seems like a desperately trying to be funny way to describe something about the winter holidays, "A fourth emerged from a nearby home with a quart of eggnog, which was inserted into Andersons mouth. The carton was held in place until drained." - this is also sesquipedalian loquaciousness instead of proper tone, which'd be "A fourth emerged from a nearby home with a quart of eggnog, which he forced Agent Anderson to ingest." and "The original instance of SCP-784-1 proceeded to [REDACTED] Paulsen with approximately three pounds of nearby snow", which is a really really cheesy joke.
It also bugs me that none of the agents actually defended themselves effectively against what does seem like normal, insane people.

There's also the issue with the article's content - I can't believe noone apparently tried to remove individuals from the town to see how they behave outside of the anomalous zone, or interrogate one. No need to even put a log , just have a sentence or two speaking about it…. as is here, there seems to have been zero actual research done which makes one wonder why do we actually bother sending people in rather than walling it off and forgetting about it.
More than that.. do we have census data? How many people are there? Do new ones get born? Do people die? How does the community behave in any of those events? Why haven't we considered unmanned exploration?

All in all, the more I look at it, the more I like the opinion that this is a -J article in mainlist.
As a -J I might even have upvoted, but, even though this is genuinely anomalous, I don't think the way it's treated has enough depth to fit in mainlist - it's pretty much written for laughs.

My main goal was to create containment procedures that would be both fairly inconspicuous for a gated community (and this is a pretty ridiculously gated community) and would also keep people from getting in or out. Evacuating the entire town couldn't be done without arousing suspicion.

I've made a minor edit to the containment procedures which addresses the issues with people needing to patrol constantly.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This was exactly my issue. Whether or not it's an isolated neighborhood in a residential area, or one next to other neighborhoods, it's still an incredible security risk. 784-1 have demonstrated that they'll abduct anybody unfortunate enough to wander in, and every month they get drunk and try to leave, with the best solution being to somehow convincing them to drink some sedative-filled eggnog. Whether or not it's working at the moment, such a potentially dangerous anomaly should have way more than the single procedure to deal with this, especially in the event that they remember to not drink the same eggnog that knocked them out every other month that it happened before.

I also have a problem with the fact that any car could just pass by the gate and see the constantly prevalent snow.

EDIT: I missed that you addressed the procedural issues since I last read it, and I'll give you that that at least provides a viable, temporary solution.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I find myself really disliking this, probably more so than it deserves. There are some really weird things going on tonally ("Christmas Spirit" and "Noel Event" in particular), but what bugs me the most is the containment strategy. Unless I missed something major, these are more or less ordinary humans we're dealing with - so why the hell are we allowing this phenomenon to endanger active residential zones? Just as one example, wouldn't it make more sense to erect a full containment site around the affected area and evacuate the surrounding neighborhoods via Eminent Domain or the like? I have to think that relying on a good lock and more electric fencing would be a fair sight more secure than throwing a carefully choreographed caroling / cover-up task force at the problem.

And even if I am missing something such that a simple lockdown of the area wouldn't be enough, that still doesn't explain why the nearby neighborhoods haven't been evacuated. Hell, if anything evacuation would be an even more obvious precaution.

Given how the concept strikes me, I doubt I'll ever like this SCP, but if you rethink some of this I may be able to at least tolerate it…
